0.headline: Sahajanand Medical Technologies IPO allotment today; GMP at 7%, check status on BSE, NSE and registrar
0.heading: Sahajanand Medical Technologies IPO allotment today; GMP at 7%, check status on BSE, NSE and registrar
0.intro: The allotment of Sahajanand Medical Technologies' initial public offering (IPO) is expected to be finalised on October 21, following a strong response from investors during the three-day subscription period.
0.body:
The allotment of Sahajanand Medical Technologies' initial public offering (IPO) is expected to be finalised on October 21, following a strong response from investors during the three-day subscription period.

The Rs 475.48-crore IPO was subscribed 14.20 times by the close of bidding on October 19, according to NSE data. The issue received bids for 13,84,72,771 shares against 97,50,482 shares on offer.

Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) led the demand, subscribing to their allotted portion 34.70 times. The non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 14.64 times, while the retail investor portion received bids for 3.03 times the shares reserved for the category.

Read Also: 'From 2 crore investors to over 13 crore in 10 years': Zerodha's Nithin Kamath credits Jio for India's retail investing boom

In the grey market, Sahajanand Medical Technologies shares were commanding a premium of nearly 7 percent on October 21, according to InvestorGain. Grey market premium (GMP) is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment and does not guarantee listing gains.

The company's shares are scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on October 23.

Sahajanand Medical Technologies IPO allotment status: How to check

Investors can check their allotment status online through the registrar's website or the stock exchanges once the results are made available.

Check allotment status on the registrar's website

Step 1. Visit the MUFG Intime public issues portal at https://in.mpms.mufg.com/Initial_Offer/public-issues.html
Step 2. Navigate to the IPO allotment status section.
Step 3. Select Sahajanand Medical Technologies from the issue list, if available.
Step 4. Enter the required details, such as PAN or application number, and submit.
Step 5. Your allotment status will be displayed once the results are published.

Check allotment status on BSE

1. Visit the BSE IPO application status page at https://www.bseindia.com/investors/appli_check
2. Select 'Equity' as the issue type.
3. Choose Sahajanand Medical Technologies from the IPO list.
4. Enter your application number or PAN, as requested.
5. Submit the details to view the status.

Check IPO bid details on NSE

Step 1. Go to the NSE IPO bid verification page at https://www.nseindia.com/invest/check-trades-bids-verify-ipo-bids
Step 2. Follow the instructions to verify your IPO bid details.
Step 3. Enter the information requested on the page.
Step 4. Your allotment status will be displayed once the results are published.

The IPO was open for subscription from October 15 to October 19. The company is raising Rs 475.48 crore entirely through an offer for sale (OFS) of approximately 1.38 crore equity shares.

Since the issue is entirely an OFS, the proceeds from the sale will go to the selling shareholders, and Sahajanand Medical Technologies will not receive the money raised through the offering.

The price band was fixed at Rs 327 to Rs 344 per share. The minimum application consisted of 43 shares, requiring an investment of Rs 14,792 at the upper end of the price band.

Check IPO News Here

Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, Avendus Capital, HSBC Securities and Capital Markets (India), and Nuvama Wealth Management are the merchant bankers to the issue.

Ahead of the public issue, Sahajanand Medical Technologies raised Rs 140.06 crore from anchor investors. The company allotted approximately 40.71 lakh equity shares to eight institutional investors on October 14 at the upper end of the price band.

Five domestic mutual fund houses, Nippon Life India, DSP Mutual Fund, WhiteOak Capital, Invesco India and UTI AMC, received around 30.25 lakh shares worth approximately Rs 104 crore through seven schemes.

Other participants in the anchor book included Allianz Global Investors Fund, Tata AIA Life Insurance Company and Natixis International Funds.

About Sahajanand Medical Technologies

Mumbai-headquartered Sahajanand Medical Technologies develops medical devices used in cardiovascular and vascular interventions. Its portfolio includes coronary stents and coronary balloons, as well as structural heart products such as transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) devices and occluders.

The company also offers renal stents under its own brand and peripheral drug-coated balloons (DCBs). Its products are used in procedures aimed at treating cardiovascular conditions and other vascular disorders.

1.headline: Jio IPO: Antique sees 17% upside, says 15% tariff hike could unlock Rs 190 per share
1.heading: Jio IPO: Antique sees 17% upside, says 15% tariff hike could unlock Rs 190 per share
1.intro: Antique expects Jio's EBITDA to grow at a compound annual growth rate of more than 15% between FY26 and FY29
1.body:
As the record-setting Jio Platforms IPO draws strong investor demand, Antique Stock Broking has recommended subscribing to the Rs 30,213-crore issue, citing seven growth drivers for the telecom and digital services business.

The brokerage sees around 17% upside in the stock and estimates that a 15% tariff hike could unlock Rs 190 per share in value.

Antique expects Jio's EBITDA to grow at a compound annual growth rate of more than 15% between FY26 and FY29. At 15.6 times EV/EBITDA, Jio's valuation is broadly in line with Bharti Airtel India at around 15.7 times, but below Bharti Hexacom at 17.7 times, the brokerage said.

Tariff hikes and subscriber migration

Jio's average revenue per user (ARPU) is around 22% lower than Bharti Airtel's, leaving room for growth as the industry raises tariffs towards an ARPU of Rs 300, Antique said. The migration of five crore JioBharat users to smartphones could provide another boost to ARPU.

Between March 2021 and March 2026, Jio added 9.82 crore subscribers, compared with Bharti Airtel's 5.19 crore. Antique also highlighted the opportunity to convert the 26.1 crore users in India who are still on 2G networks to smartphones.

Home broadband and enterprise services

Jio had 2.86 crore home services connections, nearly twice Bharti Airtel's base. It accounted for 62% of industry net additions in the first quarter of FY27, according to Antique. ARPU per home connection is 2.5 times that of a mobile connection, while the brokerage estimates a pre-tax internal rate of return of 26% for Jio's AirFiber business.

The brokerage also pointed to the growth potential in digital and enterprise services. India's digital services market is valued at Rs 5.1 lakh crore and is estimated to grow at 18% annually through FY31. Digital services penetration among the country's 7.9 crore micro, small and medium enterprises remains below 3%, while more than 90% of banks use Jio's services, Antique said.

Technology exports and infrastructure

Jio has 7,220 patent applications, which Antique sees as a potential source of value beyond its domestic telecom business. The brokerage estimates a one-time technology export opportunity of Rs 19.7 lakh crore and said the company's first overseas contract could act as a rerating trigger.

Antique also highlighted Jio's infrastructure, including 3.6 lakh telecom towers, more than 10 lakh route-km of fibre network and 5G spectrum across all three bands in all 22 telecom circles. Around 53% of its customers are on 5G, while capital expenditure as a share of revenue declined from 49% in FY24 to 23% in FY26.

Taken together, the brokerage sees tariff increases, subscriber migration, growth in home broadband and enterprise services, and the potential monetisation of technology capabilities as key drivers for Jio Platforms.

2.headline: 'From 2 crore investors to over 13 crore in 10 years': Zerodha's Nithin Kamath credits Jio for India's retail investing boom
2.heading: 'From 2 crore investors to over 13 crore in 10 years': Zerodha's Nithin Kamath credits Jio for India's retail investing boom
2.intro: As the Jio Platforms IPO opened for subscription on October 21, Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath reflected on how the telecom operator's expansion helped transform India's digital economy and contributed to the growth of online-first businesses, including his stockbroking platform.
2.body:
As the Jio Platforms IPO opened for subscription on October 21, Zerodha founder Nithin Kamath reflected on how the telecom operator's expansion helped transform India's digital economy and contributed to the growth of online-first businesses, including his stockbroking platform.

In a post on X, Kamath linked the growth of India's retail investor base to the expansion of affordable internet access, Aadhaar and the Unified Payments Interface (UPI). He said Jio, along with Bharti Airtel, helped bring millions of Indians online, creating conditions that supported the expansion of digital businesses and capital markets.

"In 2016, India had roughly 2 crore unique investors. Today, over 13 crore Indians invest in the markets, and Jio played a big part in that," Kamath wrote.

His remarks come as investors begin bidding for Jio Platforms' initial public offering (IPO), bringing the company's role in India's digital transformation into focus alongside its plans to tap the capital markets.

Kamath said Zerodha's growth depended not only on its own business model but also on the wider digital infrastructure that made online services accessible to more people.

"Zerodha wouldn't be what it is today without Aadhaar and UPI. But just as important was Jio, along with Airtel, bringing millions of Indians online with affordable data," he wrote.

Affordable mobile data lowered a key barrier to accessing internet-based services, while digital identity and payments infrastructure helped simplify customer onboarding and transactions. Together, these developments created opportunities for businesses that could reach customers through digital platforms rather than relying entirely on physical distribution networks.

For online stockbrokers, wider internet access made it easier to serve customers beyond traditional financial centres. The shift also coincided with the expansion of digital payments, increased smartphone adoption and a surge in retail participation in equity markets following the COVID-19 pandemic.

Kamath argued that this combination of infrastructure was important to the expansion of India's capital markets after the pandemic.

"Together, all of this made the huge expansion of Indian capital markets after COVID possible," he said, adding that many online-first businesses would be significantly smaller without this digital infrastructure.

Kamath also looked back at the period when Jio was preparing to enter the telecom market, recalling an Economic Times list of 10 businessmen to watch in 2016.

"When Jio was getting ready to launch in 2015, I remember being petrified to find myself on this Economic Times list of 10 businessmen to watch in 2016. Mukesh Ambani was #1 and I was #6, mainly because we had just made delivery brokerage free," he wrote.

When Jio was getting ready to launch in 2015, I remember being petrified to find myself on this Economic Times list of 10 businessmen to watch in 2016. Mukesh Ambani was #1, and I was #6, mainly because we had just made delivery brokerage free. We were, and still are, ants compared to Reliance/Jio. 😅
Looking back, what's phenomenal isn't just how big it has become. It's how much it has changed India and helped so many businesses start and grow.

We've been beneficiaries too. @Zerodha wouldn't be what it is today without Aadhaar and UPI. But just as important was Jio, along with Airtel, bringing millions of Indians online with affordable data.

Together, all of this made the huge expansion of Indian capital markets after COVID possible. Without this digital infrastructure, many online-first businesses would be much smaller, and a lot of today's consumer business models might not exist at all.

In 2016, India had roughly 2 crore unique investors. Today, over 13 crore Indians invest in the markets, and Jio played a big part in that.

I can't tell you whether to apply for the upcoming IPO. But both telcos have played a huge role in enabling an entire generation of Indian businesses like ours. And it's nice that the capital markets they helped grow can now help Jio raise money.

From the outside, it's easy to miss how much of our success depends on infrastructure built by others.

— Nithin Kamath (@Nithin0dha) October 21, 2026


Zerodha built its business around discount broking, including a zero-brokerage model for equity delivery trades. The broader shift towards digital investing helped such platforms reach a larger pool of customers, although their growth has also depended on pricing, technology, product offerings and investor participation.

Kamath stopped short of offering a view on whether investors should subscribe to the Jio Platforms IPO. Instead, he highlighted what he described as the relationship between digital infrastructure, business growth and capital formation.

"I can't tell you whether to apply for the upcoming IPO. But both telcos have played a huge role in enabling an entire generation of Indian businesses like ours. And it's nice that the capital markets they helped grow can now help Jio raise money," he wrote.

Kamath concluded by highlighting the role of external infrastructure in business success.

"From the outside, it's easy to miss how much of our success depends on infrastructure built by others," he said.
